primary_source.title: Inequalities for a Pair of Maps S x S -> S with S a Finite Set

theorem_statement_relevant: The paper defines several expansiveness notions for pairs of finite-set maps phi,psi:SxS->S and proves direct-product transfer theorems. In particular, Theorem 1 states that the direct product of component pairs satisfying the corresponding strong expansiveness hypotheses retains the product expansiveness property; Theorems 2-3 give weaker variants. In the Boolean case the paper classifies expansive pairs of Boolean operations and derives union/intersection and symmetric-difference/intersection cardinality/weight inequalities.
exact_model_assumptions: Total binary maps on finite sets, usually considered in pairs; direct products are total coordinatewise products. The strongest transfer theorem requires the paper's M-expansiveness hypotheses on each coordinate component.
resource_required: A total coordinate completion of the JANUS signed partial union together with a second map/weight choice for which the required local expansiveness hypothesis can actually be verified.
candidate_janus_insertion_point: Theorem-side abstraction of signed parent-tail interaction as a direct product of six local coordinate channels. Potentially use a conflict-completed alphabet {OMIT,POS,NEG,CONFLICT} and seek a companion map or weight that recovers omission/support information while retaining an Ahlswede-Daykin expansiveness property.
applicability: HIGH STRUCTURAL MATCH. The newly derived JANUS code-pair capacity proof already reasons coordinate-by-coordinate and multiplies local output alphabets; Ahlswede-Daykin is classical primary literature built precisely around direct-product preservation of finite-operation inequalities.
non_applicability: The JANUS resolvent operation is partial on {OMIT,POS,NEG}: opposite signs reject the pair as tautological instead of producing an ordinary output. Completing the map with a CONFLICT symbol changes the codomain and may weaken the bound. No companion operation/weight satisfying the published hypotheses has yet been proved for the exact JANUS channel. Therefore no Ahlswede-Daykin numeric inequality is imported into N58 at this stage.

related_primary.title: An Inequality for the Weights of Two Families of Sets, Their Unions and Intersections
related_primary.relevance: Four-functions style weighted inequality for two set families and their union/intersection images; useful as a weight-design template, but its direct unweighted use with an injective union map is not stronger than the current N58 argument.
